newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Brent edges up, correction higher seen.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Brent edges up, correction higher seen.

text.p: SIMEX Brent futures edged up in late afternoon dealings on Monday on slight volume, helped by a perception the market will correct higher.
Brent December was last traded at $22.55 per barrel, up five cents from London's settlement on Friday of $22.50.
Brokers said the market had shrugged off weekend news of a U.S. jet firing a missile on an Iraq air-defense unit, which Iraq later denied.

A statement Friday by the United States' United Nations Ambassador Madeleine Albright that Iraq was making "outrageous demands" on how to implement the oil-for-food deal was also ignored, brokers said.
But they said players expected to relief to the downside and for prices to move higher.
A broker said December could rise as far as $22.90 per barrel before finding resistance.
NYMEX December crude, which fell 32 cents to $23.03 per barrel in New York on Friday, was last traded at $23.17 per barrel on the after-hours ACCESS system.
